terra.problem: The borrowed-ladder joke puts down most people as unable to return what they borrow.
The text says Hanun's father died, but does not say he had just died.
Saying the half-shaving was made to be noticed assigns a motive the text does not give. Marking it as a guess does not permit an invented reason.
The passage says the Ammonites realized they had become a stench to David; it does not state that David was angry.
Saying there was no panic assigns a state of mind the text does not give.
The passage does not say David was absent from the field or that he only went out personally later.
The explanation invents a reason for Joab's choice and calls the selected men his strongest group. The text says he selected some of Israel's best men, not that this group was stronger than the rest.
The text calls the men some of Israel's best, but does not state Joab's reason for selecting them.
The passage does not say the army was listening to Joab's words.
The text says the Arameans fled before Joab; it does not establish that they never stood and fought or how short the battle was.
The passage says David went to Helam, but does not say he stayed there.
The passage does not say whether the kings joined the Ammonites in the city. It simply does not mention them doing so.
The passage says the Arameans were afraid to help the Ammonites anymore; saying the help was gone and the Arameans were out of the picture goes beyond that.
Saying the Ammonites were left without those helpers goes beyond the text's statement that the Arameans were afraid to help them anymore.
